title: Waiver and preservation of objections
summary: Waiver or forfeiture can prevent a party from relying on an objection that was available earlier. The consequences depend on the kind of objection and the governing rule.
notes: Consent can support personal jurisdiction, while the parties cannot confer missing subject-matter authority by agreement. Finality of a completed judgment raises additional questions; Capron is not a complete statement of every collateral-attack rule.

sections.Meaning: Waiver or forfeiture can prevent a party from relying on an objection that was available earlier. The consequences depend on the kind of objection and the governing rule.
sections.How to work through the question: Distinguish subject-matter jurisdiction from personal jurisdiction and other defenses. For Rule 12 objections, identify when the party first responded and which defenses had to be included then. For other defenses or procedural rights, examine the specific preservation requirement and prejudice analysis in the assigned decisions.
